evidence.note: Claim: the loop detectors (repeated_failure, gate_flapping, repeat_claims) surface only in 'ddflow loops', doctor and the item brief, not in the cadenced 'ddflow health' pass. Probed: wrote tests/test_health_watch_liveness.py asserting a 3x-identical-failure gate run yields a RUNAWAY finding; it FAILED on unfixed main ([]) and PASSED after adding services.healthwatch._loop_runaways.

r-everything-configurable respected (thresholds stay [loops].max_repeated_failures etc.); r-bounded-everything (reuses existing loop thresholds, no new loop); no new knob, no I/O in core.health; the change is read-only wiring over core.progress.loops.
committed 181c303c5: healthwatch.inspect now appends _loop_runaways() Findings (RUNAWAY) from core.progress.loops.detect(); regression test added/verified.

chunk_findings.detail: `_loop_runaways` emits every matching loop as `H.RUNAWAY` with the same holder, then `inspect` dedupes with `{f.key: f for f in found}` by `(kind, item, holder)` as that function states. Two findings for one held item (for example `repeated_failure` on `unit_tests` and `gate_flapping`, or `repeat_claims` plus `repeated_failure`) share that key, so the dict keeps only the later one and drops the other loop’s `detail`, `count`, `threshold`, and `gate`. A lane that is both flapping and re-failing the same gate therefore shows a single RUNAWAY, and which breach survives depends only on `LPS.detect` order.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_loop_runaways

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier dedupe bug is only half fixed. `inspect` still collapses with `{f.key: f for f in found}` on `(kind, item, holder)`, and the new holder is `f.gate or f.kind` (about line 78), not loop-kind plus gate. Two `LPS.detect` hits on the same item that share a non-empty gate — `repeated_failure` on `unit_tests` and `gate_flapping` on `unit_tests` — both become `H.RUNAWAY` / item / holder `unit_tests`, so the dict keeps only the later `detail`, `count`, `threshold`, and `loop`. The new test only runs two `repeated_failure`s on different gates, which get different holders and never hits this input. `repeat_claims` plus a gated `repeated_failure` is separated only because one gate is empty; any pair with the same gate still drops a loop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_loop_runaways
